title: closure-provider-pr-context-corrective-20260730
outOfScope: Rewriting closed PR #474, #477, or #478 archive evidence.
Deleting any branch until the corrected closure command verifies the exact merged PR.
Changing release behavior, installer behavior, or provider merge authority.

sources.reason: The --worktree adapter scopes Git commands but currently leaves gh PR discovery in the invoking worktree.
Executable closure regressions establish side-effect and provider-query expectations.
Authoritative provider record: the target branch is merged, despite unscoped gh discovery reporting otherwise.
Authoritative user-facing closure behavior and stop conditions.

rawUserRequest: Continue the authorized plan. A merged Work Item closure was blocked because the selected worktree was not used for GitHub PR discovery. Fix workflow defects before release, with executable regression protection and full governed lifecycle.

declaredIntent.summary: Bind GitHub pull-request discovery to the selected Work Item branch during exceptional worktree closure.

riskAssessment.reason: An incorrect PR lookup could block a valid closure or, if weakened, target the wrong provider record and branch.

executionDecision.reason: The user authorized continuing planned corrective Work Items, PR lifecycle, and cleanup without per-item pauses.

checkpointPolicy.reason: Record at least one checkpoint before finishing to reduce mid-task drift.

acceptance: A1: When --worktree is supplied, PR discovery queries the selected worktree's head branch rather than the invoking worktree branch.
A2: The selected branch and PR Head SHA must exactly match; a missing, open, or mismatched PR stops before receipt generation or cleanup.
A3: Regression tests cover a merged child Work Item whose invoking worktree is on a different branch, proving the provider query uses the child branch.
A4: English and Japanese closure guidance preserve the selected-worktree PR binding and fail-closed boundary.
A5: The closure provider command deterministically selects `codex/<task>` before checking the authoritative merged PR result; the post-merge #474 closure remains a separate lifecycle action.
guidelines: New public APIs must be documented.
Do not import internal modules from other features.

intent.problem: The worktree adapter only prefixes Git commands with -C. It leaves gh pr view unscoped, so a closure invoked from a synchronized parent worktree inspects that parent PR rather than the requested child Work Item PR. This falsely reports a merged child PR as unmerged and prevents required cleanup.
constraints: Do not weaken PR state, branch, Head SHA, base, receipt, or cleanup verification.
Do not rewrite closed archive evidence or delete a branch without provider-verified merged ownership.
Keep GitHub CLI use explicit and deterministic for the selected branch.
intent.rationale: Provider verification must bind to the exact selected Work Item branch; otherwise closure is not a reliable lifecycle control.

scenarioCoverage.scenario: A merged child Work Item is closed with --worktree while the invoking worktree is checked out on its parent branch.
scenarioCoverage.expected: The provider adapter queries the child's branch and accepts the merged child PR only when branch and Head SHA exactly match.
scenarioCoverage.verificationPlan: Add a lifecycle regression that captures the gh command and asserts it supplies the selected branch explicitly.

scenarioCoverage.scenario: The selected child branch has no merged PR, or its provider Head SHA differs from the local branch.
scenarioCoverage.expected: Closure stops before receipt generation, remote deletion, or local branch deletion.
scenarioCoverage.verificationPlan: Retain and run existing fail-closed PR verification regressions alongside the new selected-branch regression.
